characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Scanning electron microscope (JEOL 6500) equipped with an EBSD system; HKL Channel 5 system software
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 5 s⁻¹ (ε = 2, 1100 °C) the map shows large equiaxed original grains with a sparse red (subgrain) boundary network, plus a strongly elongated grain and a band of fine grains with dense red boundary segments (shear/deformation band) — a mixture of young recrystallized grains and old deformed grains indicating DDRX.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Analyses performed near the surface (0.9 radius); observation plane θz, z-axis parallel to the vertical direction in the EBSD maps; black lines = grain boundaries (θ ≥ 15°), red lines = subgrain boundaries (2° ≤ θ < 15°)
characterization_methods.purpose: Illustrate the microstructures of samples deformed by torsion at ε = 2, 1100 °C and 5 s⁻¹

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD-derived; compared with the MacKenzie random (cubic) distribution
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 1100 °C and 5 s⁻¹: LAB : 20%, HAB : 80%, average misorientation angle 33.1°; the distribution is close to the MacKenzie random distribution with few LABs and a maximum number of HABs near 45°.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 1100 °C; strain rate 5 s⁻¹; LAB/HAB divider at 15°
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify the misorientation distribution to evidence DDRX

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD-based orientation analysis of recrystallized grains with internal misorientation below 2°
characterization_methods.key_findings: The recrystallized grains formed at 5 s⁻¹ carry only a weak {110} texture (max = 1.77), i.e. no preferred orientation.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the texture of DDRX recrystallized grains
characterization_methods.technique: {110} pole figure texture analysis of selected recrystallized grains (Fig. 6)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: A DDRX nucleus is a small volume of material containing a low density of dislocations and separated from the surrounding matrix by HABs; nuclei usually appear near original grain boundaries. At 1100 °C and 5 s⁻¹ the misorientation distribution is HAB-dominated (LAB : 20%, HAB : 80%).

interfaces.phase_evolution: The initial deformed structure is quickly replaced by a recrystallized one; new grains grow at the expense of old hardened grains (grain-boundary migration decreases the elastic energy), preventing the initiation of the slower CDRX process.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot torsion test at 1100 °C, strain rate 5 s⁻¹ and ε = 2, performed in a direction involving a negative shear, under argon atmosphere to reduce the oxidation phenomena.
Quenched immediately after deformation to retain the microstructures and avoid post-dynamic recrystallization.

defects.lattice_distortion: old grains display internal misorientations (red lines); freshly recrystallized grains are free of substructure
defects.type: subgrain boundaries / low-angle boundaries (red lines, 2° ≤ θ < 15°)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: bimodal mixture of large elongated old (deformed) grains and small equiaxed freshly recrystallized grains
grain_structure.texture: recrystallized grains carry only a weak texture ({110} pole figure max = 1.77), i.e. no preferred orientation

phases_present.morphology: mixture of small equiaxed freshly recrystallized grains and large elongated original grains
phases_present.texture: recrystallized grains have no preferred orientations (very low / weak {110} texture)

structures.overall_structure: Microstructure appears as a mixture of 'young' freshly recrystallized grains (small, equiaxed, free of substructure) and 'old' original grains (large, elongated along the shear direction, displaying internal misorientations / red lines), evidencing discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX). The initial 100% recrystallized equiaxed starting microstructure (~800 µm grain size) is progressively replaced by a much finer recrystallized one.

unmapped_findings: For the 1100 °C / 5 s⁻¹ / ε = 2 condition, the DDRX mechanism is activated: at high temperature and high strain rate, the Fe–8% Al ferritic alloy undergoes discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX), whereas at lower temperature and strain rate continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) occurs.

According to the strain rate–temperature map (Fig. 7), at 1100 °C the DDRX-activated domain lies above a temperature-dependent threshold of about 0.1–0.2 s⁻¹, so the 5 s⁻¹ condition falls within the DDRX-activated domain.

At these high strain rates the duration of the tests is shorter, dynamic recovery is less effective, strain hardening is stronger, and the stored elastic energy provides a sufficient driving force for nucleation and growth of new grains.
Recrystallized grains produced by DDRX display random orientations (no preferred orientation), which the authors suggest is advantageous to limit the roping surface-defect phenomenon in hot rolling.
The initial (pre-deformation) state of the alloy is 100% recrystallized with equiaxed grains of ~800 µm and is morphologically isotropic; this starting state is common to all torsion conditions.
